claims.statement: Closure guide declares FPT/GHEC/GHES; opener may close own issue, repository owner/personal-repository collaborators and organization triage-or-greater may close others. GHEC EMU shared qualifier confines changes to enterprise repositories.

Closing may signal fixed/actioned or not-planned work; chosen reason is lifecycle metadata, not fresh evidence that acceptance criteria passed. The guide also points to keyword-based automatic closure.
UI selects target issue, optionally selects close reason and closes it. This capability does not override this project human-only closure rule or authorize blanket closing of tracked work.

Linked PR default-branch merge automatically closes linked issue; description keywords are interpreted only for default-branch targets. Other target branches ignore keywords/create no links and have no issue-closure effect.

Keyword families close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed and resolve/resolves/resolved allow uppercase and colons. Same-repository numbers and explicit owner/repository identities differ; each of multiple references needs full syntax.

Guide states keyword reference to another PR comment links PRs and merging referencing PR also closes referenced PR. Actual target identity/behavior require separate runtime verification; linking is not accepted completion.

Keyword links require description edit to remove keyword; only manual links can be manually unlinked. Commit-message keywords close on default-branch integration without listing containing PR as linked PR.

PR-sidebar manual links require write, allow up to ten issues per PR and same repository. Issue-sidebar manual links require write but allow different-repository PR/branch and remember last selected repository; preflight must verify exact destination, not reuse remembered scope.

Default-branch integration and automatic close are lifecycle events, not evidence of tests, enforcement, deployment, recovery or independent acceptance. Examples were not executed and project uses non-closing refs.

Duplicate timeline event requires commenter write access at repository where reference comment is created. A new Duplicate-of-number comment or provided saved reply establishes relationship; ordinary similarity does not establish semantic equivalence.
Undo unmarks duplicate and records another timeline event; guide does not promise deletion of original comment/history or general restoration of issue state.
Marking duplicate is distinct from closure and from audited claim deduplication. Guide supplies no automatic closure guarantee or independent acceptance of either referenced work item.
